require not mem[..] << 40 style range checks: 24 lines, unchanged.

Parameters are now named by calldata word: onRegister's flag is _param7 (offset 196); onAfterRemoveLiquidity uses _param5.._param8, onAfterAddLiquidity _param4, _param5, _param7, _param8; onAfterInitialize _param1, _param3.

regressions.function: getReClammPoolDynamicData() (0x2c357688), onBeforeInitialize, setCenterednessMargin, stop/startPriceRatioUpdate and other Vault-calling functions
regressions.old: _16 = mem[64] / mem[_16 + ceil32(min(32, return_data.size))] = 0xe4dc2aa4... / if ceil32(min(32, return_data.size)) + mem[64] > 18446744073709551615 ...
regressions.source: ReClammPool.sol:getReClammPoolDynamicData, successive Vault calls whose returns are abi-decoded into memory
regressions.issue: The free pointer is now resolved, which fixes the aliasing (mem[192] = ext_call.return_data[0] instead of mem[_16]), but its value is printed inline as a 5- to 8-term sum at every use. 227 lines now carry six-term address sums (3 before), and each Panic(65) check repeats it three times.
regressions.rule: When a resolved free-pointer value is used more than a few times, bind it to a variable at the mem[64] read (_16 = 32 * _2 + ... + 800) and print the addresses relative to that variable. This keeps the aliasing precision.

regressions.source: ReClammPool.sol getReClammPoolDynamicData: return of the ReClammPoolDynamicData struct
regressions.issue: _4400 holds mem[64], and nothing writes mem[64] before these lines, yet _4400 - mem[64] is no longer folded to 0. The copy-loop bound re-reads the length word instead of _4406, and the return lost the head words the old text listed. Values are unchanged (checked by hand).
regressions.rule: A variable bound to a read of mem[64] equals any later read of mem[64] as long as no write to mem[64] comes between, so fold x - mem[64] to 0. Use the bound length variable as the loop bound when the length word is not written in the loop.

improvements: Hex constants whole bytes (1100+ lines). Durations: 25 * 10**13 * 3600 now 9 * 10**17. Free pointer resolved: event data, two selectors and all emitAuxiliaryEvent bytes arguments decoded. Typed array returns in getCurrentLiveBalances, computeInitialBalancesRaw, getTokens and getTokenInfo (4 arrays, 2 copy loops gone). Two early-return arms of getReClammPoolDynamicData now return the full struct field by field, removing 6 copy loops. Bubbled reverts print as revert with ext_call.return_data. Dominated checks dropped: onSwap's Panic(33) (decode already requires kind < 2), and setCenterednessMargin's repeated Panic(50) and PoolOutsideTargetRange checks inside the arm known to have balance0 != 0. FixedPoint products shown with SafeMath.mul3. Text is 5% smaller (3.31M to 3.13M chars).
notes: Diff of 16k lines, mostly function reordering. Per-function changes total about 3,000 lines, so reviewed by structure: for each of the 27 changed functions, the counts of whiles, calls, logs, reverts, storage writes and returns, compared old vs new, with every count change traced. Removed: whiles 46->34 (return-encoding copies became Array returns or structured returns); reverts in onSwap (Panic(33), dominated), setCenterednessMargin (4 Panic(50), 1 mulDiv panic, 2 PoolOutsideTargetRange; all dominated by checks of the same values on the enclosing path, new 13855-13858). Added: computeCurrentPriceRatio and computeCurrentFourthRootPriceRatio gain an explicit add check (10**18 > b + 10**18) before the unchanged product check, correct and slightly redundant. stagecheck --function 0x0673d09a (4 seeds, 32 per selector): 160 same, but all revert at the Vault call to 0x0, so the deep paths were checked by reading only. Pack header has no regex pattern line, so P1-P6 are 0 (round 1: P2 1, P6 3).
summary: No semantic regression found. Readability gained a lot (aliasing resolved, typed and structured returns, emitAuxiliaryEvent decoded, parameter names fixed, 12 copy loops gone). The cost is long inline free-pointer sums on 227 lines and a rawer main-path return in getReClammPoolDynamicData. The two aborts remain.
